title: Tor amplitude under comparison for Noetherian coefficients
statement:
Let $X$ be quasi-compact and quasi-separated, $\Lambda$ a discrete Noetherian
ring and $K\in D^b_c(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$. For integers $a\leq b$, $K$ has Tor
amplitude in $[a,b]$ (that is, $K\otimes^{\mathrm L}_\Lambda N$ has cohomology
only in degrees $[a,b]$ for every $\Lambda$-module sheaf $N$ on $X_{\Et}$) if and
only if $\nu_X^*K$ has Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$ on $X_{\Proet}$. Consequently
$\nu_X^*$ restricts to an equivalence
$D^b_{\mathrm{ctf}}(X_{\Et},\Lambda)\simeq\Dctf(X,\Lambda)$.

proof.text: Obtain the canonical derived comparison and the bounded constructible equivalence from constructibleComparison.

Use the proved coefficient-model flat criterion to represent an etale Tor interval by a flat complex in exactly that interval. Pull it back termwise; flatness preservation and zero-object preservation retain flatness and support. The localization factorization identifies this model with D(K). The reverse flat criterion proves all pro-etale tensor tests.

Choose an etale K-flat representative with flat terms of K by the proved coefficient-model flat-resolution theorem. Its termwise comparison pullback is K-flat by the flat-pullback bridge and represents D(K) by the localization factorization. Apply the pro-etale Tor interval to this representative and the inverse image of each etale test module. Ordinary single-test reflection gives etale tensor-test vanishing for the chosen representative. The proved coefficient-model tensor-test isomorphism transports it to every K-flat representative of K.

Tor amplitude is invariant under derived isomorphism by composition of representative isomorphisms. Restrict the constructible equivalence to the finite-Tor full subcategories. Full faithfulness is inherited, and its counit, the interval reflection, and essential surjectivity supply finite-Tor antecedents. The restricted forward functor is identified with D by whiskering the given natural comparison.
